newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares regained some of their earlier losses just before the close of trade on short-covering after hitting day lows in the afternoon in the wake of weaker world markets, dealers said Friday.
However, gold shares drifted off their day highs at the close despite a firmer bullion price.
The industrial index recovered from 70 points down in afternoon trade to close 40.3 points off at 8,042.8.
"It has been hectic these last few minutes. There has been a lot of short-covering, all punters are getting out of the market," a dealer said.

Industrials were hit by a poor Wall Street at open which lost 94.28 points to 6,755.75 points on Thursday night. The fall encouraged arbitrage activity in the morning with players selling stock and buying the future.
"We have seen a bit of profit-taking and selling pressure right across the board," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe Generale Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.
The gold price bounced back above the $350 an ounce level on short-covering in New York on Thursday night, but dealers said the recovery would be short-lived.
Gold shares were stronger but drifted off their best levels possibly on the firmer rand, a dealer said.
The market was seen firm next week, cheered by positive occurences this week, dealers said.
The overall index lost 33.3 points to 6,684.6 and the gold index was up 17.2 points to 1,370.4 points.

The better trade surplus figure and Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' comments that the currency would be stable this year, depreciating by less than inflation differentials would boost shares, they said.
"If we see a correction on the Dow overnight, we could see a firmer market towards the end of the week," Dominick Rey, a senior dealer at Investec Fergusson Bros told Reuters.

Anglo lost 750 cents to 249 rand, SA Breweries added 25 cents to 123.50 rand, First National dropped 70 cents to 25.20 rand, Freegold was up 45 cents to 31.90 rand and Kloof gained 65 cents to 33.40 rand.
Near-dated equity industrial futures ended weak on softer world markets and golds were firmer on recovery in the bullion price.
The market will take its cue from Wall Street and the bullion price next week, dealers said.
The March all-share contract stood at 6,135/70 from 6,246, the industrial contract was at 7,802/15 from 7,935 and the gold contract was at 967/75 from 950.
